readings.title: The Dross of Israel
readings.subtitle: Jerusalem as a refining furnace for God's wrath.
readings.text: [17] And the word of <dn>YeHoVaH</dn> came to me, saying, [18] “Son of man, the house of Yisra’ěl has become dross to <dn>Me</dn>. All of them are bronze, and tin, and iron, and lead, in the midst of a furnace – they have become the dross of silver. [19] “Therefore thus said the Master <dn>YeHoVaH</dn>, <dq>‘Because all of you have become dross, therefore see, <dn>I</dn> am gathering <dn>את</dn> you into the midst of Yerushalayim.</dq> [20] <dq>As they gather <dn>את</dn> silver, and <dn>את</dn> bronze, and <dn>את</dn> iron, and <dn>את</dn> lead, and <dn>את</dn> tin into the midst of a furnace, to blow fire on it, to melt it, so <dn>I</dn> gather you in <dn>My</dn> displeasure and in <dn>My</dn> wrath. And <dn>I</dn> shall blow and melt you.</dq> [21] <dq>And <dn>I</dn> shall gather you and blow on you with the fire of <dn>My</dn> wrath, and you shall be melted in its midst.</dq> [22] <dq>As silver is melted in the midst of a furnace, so are you melted in its midst. And you shall know that <dn>I</dn>, <dn>YeHoVaH</dn>, have poured out <dn>את</dn> <dn>My</dn> wrath on you.’ ”</dq>

readings.title: A Corrupt Land Without an Intercessor
readings.subtitle: The failure of prophets, priests, leaders, and the people.
readings.text: [23] And the word of <dn>YeHoVaH</dn> came to me, saying, [24] “Son of man, say to her, <dq>‘You are a land that is not cleansed or rained upon in the day of displeasure.’</dq> [25] “There is a conspiracy of her prophets in her midst, like a roaring lion tearing the prey. They have devoured life, they have taken wealth and precious matters, they have made many widows in her midst. [26] <dq>“Her priests have done violence to <dn>My</dn> teaching and they profane <dn>My</dn> set-apart matters. They have not distinguished between the set-apart and profane, nor have they made known the difference between the unclean and the clean. And they have hidden their eyes from <dn>My</dn> Sabbaths, and <dn>I</dn> am profaned in their midst.</dq> [27] “Her leaders in her midst are like wolves tearing the prey, to shed blood, to destroy lives, and to get greedy gain. [28] “And her prophets have coated them with whitewash, seeing a false vision, and divining a lie for them, saying, <dq>‘Thus said the Master <dn>YeHoVaH</dn>,’</dq> when <dn>YeHoVaH</dn> had not spoken. [29] “The people of the land have practised oppression, and committed robbery, and have wronged the poor and needy. And they oppressed the stranger without right-ruling. [30] <dq>“And <dn>I</dn> sought for a man among them who would make a wall, and stand in the breach before <dn>Me</dn> on behalf of the land, that <dn>I</dn> should not destroy it – but <dn>I</dn> did not find one!</dq> [31] <dq>“Therefore <dn>I</dn> have poured out <dn>My</dn> displeasure on them, <dn>I</dn> have consumed them with the fire of <dn>My</dn> wrath. And <dn>I</dn> have put their way on their own head,”</dq> declares the Master <dn>YeHoVaH</dn>.

readings.title: Oholah and Oholibah
readings.subtitle: The allegory of Samaria's idolatry and punishment.
readings.text: [1] And the word of <dn>YeHoVaH</dn> came to me, saying, [2] “Son of man, there were two women, daughters of one mother. [3] “And they whored in Mitsrayim, they whored in their youth. There their breasts were handled, and there their maiden nipples were squeezed. [4] “And their names were: Oholah the elder and Oholiḇah her sister. And they were <dn>Mine</dn>, and they bore sons and daughters. And their names: Shomeron is Oholah, and Yerushalayim is Oholiḇah. [5] “And Oholah whored while she was <dn>Mine</dn>. And she lusted for her lovers, the neighbouring Ashshurians, [6] dressed in purple, officers and rulers, all of them desirable young men, horsemen riding on horses. [7] “So she gave her whorings on them, all of them choice sons of Ashshur. And with all for whom she lusted, with all their idols, she defiled herself. [8] “And she did not forsake her whorings from Mitsrayim, for in her youth they had lain with her, and they squeezed her maiden nipples, and poured out their whorings on her. [9] <dq>“Therefore <dn>I</dn> have given her into the hand of her lovers, into the hand of the Ashshurians, for whom she lusted.</dq> [10] “They uncovered her nakedness, they took away her sons and daughters, and killed her with the sword. And she became a byword among women, and they executed judgments on her.

readings.title: Oholibah's Corruption
readings.subtitle: Jerusalem follows and surpasses Samaria's idolatry.
readings.text: [11] “And her sister Oholiḇah saw this, yet she became more corrupt in her lust than she, and in her whorings more corrupt than her sister’s whorings. [12] “She lusted for the sons of Ashshur, officers and rulers, the ones near, perfectly dressed, horsemen riding on horses, all of them desirable young men. [13] <dq>“And <dn>I</dn> saw that she was defiled, they both took the same way.</dq> [14] “But she increased her whorings, and she looked at men carved on the wall, images of Kasdim inscribed in red, [15] girded with belts around their loins, flowing turbans on their heads, all of them looking like officers, like the sons of Baḇel of Kasdim, the land of their birth. [16] “As soon as her eyes saw them, she lusted for them and sent messengers to them in Kasdima. [17] “And the sons of Baḇel came to her, into the bed of carnal-love, and they defiled her with their whorings. And she was defiled by them, and her being turned from them in disgust. [18] <dq>“And she uncovered her whorings and uncovered her nakedness. Then <dn>I</dn> turned <dn>My</dn> being from her in disgust, as <dn>My</dn> being had turned from her sister in disgust.</dq> [19] “And she increased her whorings, remembering the days of her youth, when she whored in the land of Mitsrayim. [20] “And she lusted after her lovers, whose flesh is like the flesh of donkeys, and whose emission is like the emission of horses. [21] “Thus you longed for the wickedness of your youth, when the Mitsrites squeezed your nipples because of the breasts of your youth.

readings.title: Judgment on Oholibah
readings.subtitle: The lovers of Jerusalem will become her destroyers.
readings.text: [22] “Therefore, Oholiḇah, thus said the Master <dn>YeHoVaH</dn>, <dq>‘See, <dn>I</dn> am stirring up <dn>את</dn> your lovers against you, from whom your being turned in disgust, and shall bring them against you from every side:</dq> [23] <dq>the children of Baḇel, and all the Kasdim, Peqoḏ, and Shova, and Qova, all the sons of Ashshur with them, all of them desirable young men, governors and rulers, officers and men of name, all of them riding on horses.</dq> [24] <dq>And they shall come against you with battle-axe, chariots, and vehicles, and with an assembly of peoples. They shall set against you armour, and shield, and helmet all around. And <dn>I</dn> shall commit <dn>את</dn> the judgment to them, and they shall judge you according to their rulings.</dq> [25] <dq>And <dn>I</dn> shall set <dn>My</dn> jealousy against you and they shall deal heatedly with you. They shall cut off your nose and your ears, while the rest of you fall by the sword. Your sons and your daughters they shall take away, while the rest of you shall be consumed by fire.</dq> [26] <dq>And they shall strip you of your garments and shall take your pretty jewels.</dq> [27] <dq>And <dn>I</dn> shall put an end to your wickedness and to your whorings from the land of Mitsrayim, so that you do not lift your eyes to them neither remember Mitsrayim any more.’</dq> [28] “For thus said the Master <dn>YeHoVaH</dn>, <dq>‘See, <dn>I</dn> am giving you into the hand of those whom you hate, into the hand of those from whom your being turned in disgust.</dq> [29] <dq>And they shall deal with you in hatred, and they shall take away all you have worked for, and they shall leave you naked and bare. And the nakedness of your whorings shall be uncovered, and the wickedness of your whorings.</dq> [30] <dq><dn>I</dn> do this to you because of your whoring after the nations, because you have been defiled by their idols.</dq> [31] <dq>You have walked in the way of your sister, and <dn>I</dn> shall give <dn>את</dn> her cup into your hand.’</dq> [32] “Thus said the Master <dn>YeHoVaH</dn>, <dq>‘Drink of your sister’s cup, the deep and wide one – you being laughed at and mocked at – for it holds much.</dq> [33] <dq>Be filled with drunkenness and sorrow, the cup of astonishment and ruin, the cup of your sister Shomeron.</dq> [34] <dq>And you shall drink it and shall drain it, and gnaw its shards, and tear at your own breasts. For <dn>I</dn> have spoken,’</dq> declares the Master <dn>YeHoVaH</dn>. [35] “Therefore thus said the Master <dn>YeHoVaH</dn>, <dq>‘Because you have forgotten <dn>Me</dn> and cast <dn>Me</dn> behind your back, therefore you shall bear <dn>את</dn> your wickedness and <dn>את</dn> your whorings.’ ”</dq>

readings.title: The Sisters Judged
readings.subtitle: Their abominations are declared, and their punishment is decreed.
readings.text: [36] And <dn>YeHoVaH</dn> said to me, <dq>“Son of man, judge <dn>את</dn> Oholah and <dn>את</dn> Oholiḇah! And declare to them <dn>את</dn> their abominations.</dq> [37] <dq>“For they have committed adultery, and blood is on their hands. And they have committed adultery with their idols, and even offered their sons whom they bore to <dn>Me</dn>, passing them through the fire, to devour.</dq> [38] <dq>“They also did this to <dn>Me</dn>: They have defiled <dn>My</dn> set-apart place on the same day, and they have profaned <dn>My</dn> Sabbaths.</dq> [39] <dq>“For when they had slain their children for their idols, on the same day they came into <dn>My</dn> set-apart place to profane it. And see, that is what they did in the midst of <dn>My</dn> House.</dq> [40] <dq>“And they even sent for men to come from afar, to whom a messenger was sent. And see, they came – for whom you washed yourself, painted your eyes, and adorned yourself with ornaments.</dq> [41] <dq>“And you sat on a splendid couch, with a table prepared before it, on which you had set <dn>My</dn> incense and <dn>My</dn> oil.</dq> [42] <dq>“And the sound of a crowd at ease was with her, and drunkards were brought from the wilderness with men of the commonest sort. And they put bracelets on their wrists and pretty crowns on their heads.</dq> [43] <dq>“Then <dn>I</dn> said concerning the one worn out in adulteries, ‘Now let them commit her whorings, even hers!’</dq> [44] <dq>“And they went in to her, as men go in to a woman who is a whore. Thus they went in to Oholah and Oholiḇah, the wicked women.</dq> [45] <dq>“But let righteous men judge them with the judgment of adulteresses, and the judgment of women who shed blood, for they are adulteresses, and blood is on their hands.</dq> [46] “For thus said the Master <dn>YeHoVaH</dn>, <dq>‘Bring up an assembly against them, give them up to maltreatment and plunder.</dq> [47] <dq>And the assembly shall stone them with stones and cut them with their swords. They shall kill their sons and their daughters, and burn their houses with fire.</dq> [48] <dq>And <dn>I</dn> shall put an end to wickedness in the land, and all the women shall be instructed not to commit wickedness as you have done.</dq> [49] <dq>And they shall put <dn>את</dn> your wickedness on you, and you shall bear the sins of your idols. And you shall know that <dn>I</dn> am the Master <dn>YeHoVaH</dn>.’ ”</dq>

readings.title: Zedekiah's Rebellion and the Siege of Jerusalem
readings.subtitle: Nebuchadnezzar encamps against the city in the ninth year of Zedekiah's reign.
readings.text: [20] ...And Tsiḏqiyahu rebelled against the sovereign of Baḇel. [2 Kings 25:1] And it came to be in the ninth year of his reign, in the tenth new moon, on the tenth of the new moon, that Neḇuḵaḏnetstsar sovereign of Baḇel and all his army came against Yerushalayim and encamped against it, and they built a siege wall against it all around. [2] And the city was besieged until the eleventh year of Sovereign Tsiḏqiyahu.

readings.title: The Siege Begins
readings.subtitle: A parallel account of Nebuchadnezzar's siege against Jerusalem.
readings.text: [3] ...until <dn>He</dn> had cast them out from <dn>His</dn> presence. And Tsiḏqiyahu rebelled against the sovereign of Baḇel. [4] And it came to be in the ninth year of his reign, in the tenth new moon, on the tenth of the new moon, that Neḇuḵaḏretstsar sovereign of Baḇel and all his army came against Yerushalayim and encamped against it. And they built a siege wall against it all around. [5] And the city was under siege until the eleventh year of Sovereign Tsiḏqiyahu.

readings.title: Jeremiah During the Siege
readings.subtitle: The prophet remains in the court of the guard as the siege begins.
readings.text: [28] ...and he was there when Yerushalayim was taken. [Jeremiah 39:1] In the ninth year of Tsiḏqiyahu sovereign of Yehuḏah, in the tenth new moon, Neḇuḵaḏretstsar sovereign of Baḇel and all his army came against Yerushalayim, and besieged it.

readings.title: The Parable of the Boiling Pot
readings.subtitle: On the very day the siege begins, Ezekiel is given a sign of Jerusalem's imminent destruction.
readings.text: [1] And in the ninth year, in the tenth new moon, on the tenth of the new moon, the word of <dn>YeHoVaH</dn> came to me, saying, [2] <dq>“Son of man, write down <dn>את</dn> the name of the day, for on this same day the sovereign of Baḇel has thrown himself against Yerushalayim.</dq> [3] <dq>“And speak a parable to the rebellious house, and you shall say to them, ‘Thus said the Master <dn>YeHoVaH</dn>, “Put on a pot, put it on, and also pour water into it.</dq> [4] <dq>“Gather pieces of meat in it, every good piece, the thigh and the shoulder, fill it with choice bones.</dq> [5] <dq>“Take the choice of the flock, also pile bones under it, cook it thoroughly, also let the bones cook in it.”</dq> [6] <dq>Therefore thus said the Master <dn>YeHoVaH</dn>, “Woe to the city of blood, to the pot in which there is rust, and whose rust has not gone out of it! Bring it out piece by piece, on which no lot has fallen.</dq> [7] <dq>“For her blood is in her midst. She has set it on a shining rock. She did not pour it on the ground, to cover it with dust.</dq> [8] <dq>“To stir up wrath and take vengeance, <dn>I</dn> have set her blood on a shining rock, so that it would not be covered.”</dq> [9] <dq>Therefore thus said the Master <dn>YeHoVaH</dn>, “Woe to the city of blood! Let <dn>Me</dn> also make the pile great.</dq> [10] <dq>“Heap on the wood, kindle the fire, cook the meat well, mixing in the spices, and let the bones be burned up.</dq> [11] <dq>“And set it on the coals, empty, so that it gets hot, and its bronze glows. And its filthiness shall be melted in it, and its rust be consumed.</dq> [12] <dq>“She has wearied herself with sorrows, and her great rust has not gone from her. Into the fire with her rust!</dq> [13] <dq>“In your filthiness is wickedness. Because <dn>I</dn> have cleansed you, but you are not clean. You shall not be cleansed of your filthiness any more, till <dn>I</dn> have caused <dn>My</dn> wrath to rest upon you.</dq> [14] <dq>“<dn>I</dn>, <dn>YeHoVaH</dn>, have spoken. It shall come, and <dn>I</dn> shall do it. <dn>I</dn> do not hold back, nor do <dn>I</dn> pardon, nor do <dn>I</dn> relent. According to your ways and according to your deeds they shall judge you,”</dq> declares the Master <dn>YeHoVaH</dn>.’ ”
